newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony Q1 entertainment sales, operating revenue up.
newsitem.headline: Sony Q1 entertainment sales, operating revenue up.

text.p: Sony Corp announced on Thursday that group sales and operating revenue from its entertainment units rose 24.3 percent to 283.82 billion yen in the three months to June 30 against the same period a year ago.
Sony's entertainment revenues come largely from its troubled Hollywood film-making unit, Sony Pictures Entertainment, and record unit, Sony Music Entertainment.

Sony said the yen's 10 percent year-on-year decline against the dollar and 16 percent drop against the pound, combined with its one percent growth against the mark, increased its April/June group sales by about 90 billion yen.

"It is estimated that sales would have been approximately 90 billion yen lower than the reported figure, if the value of the yen had remained the same as in the previous year," Sony said in its statement.
Sony also said that as a result of a change in the accounting period at its movie unit, group sales for the unit's first quarter covered the four-month period from March 1 to June 30, 1997.
In the electronics business, Sony enjoyed a 22.2 percent year-on-year increase in its group sales and operating revenue to 1.08 trillion yen, helped by the yen's general weakness.
It said sales of its 32-bit home game player, the PlayStation, also enjoyed continued growth.

By region, group sales and operating revenue in the United States topped the list at 435.89 billion yen, up 36.5 percent from the same period a year earlier, followed by 388.57 billion yen in Japan, up 16.6 percent.
Group sales and operating revenue in Europe rose 19.1 percent to 326.40 billion yen, it said.
